Nineteen patients (17 males, 2 females) with alcohol dependence (DSM-IV criteria; American Psychiatric Association, 2000 ) and 20 healthy subjects were included.

value: The total amount of alcohol consumed between baseline and follow-up MRI examination correlated negatively with GM volumes in the bilateral thalamus, occipital lobe near Brodmann Area 18, and right middle frontal and precentral gyri. The more damaged these regions were at baseline, the more alcohol patients tended to consume between baseline and follow-up.

Smaller thalamic, middle frontal, and precentral volumes at treatment entry were associated with resuming heavy alcohol consumption, suggesting that baseline structural brain volumes may provide information about treatment outcome.

spans.text: #### Longitudinal Study: Relationship Between Volumetric Changes in the Alcoholic Group and Amount of Alcohol Consumed Between Baseline and Follow-Up

definition.value: Regression analysis between GM changes and the total amount of alcohol consumed between baseline and follow-up with age as covariate (negative correlation).

spans.text: Regression analysis (SPM5) between GM changes and the total amount of alcohol consumed between baseline and follow-up with age as covariate (negative correlation; p < 0.005 uncorrected; k = 100 voxels; displayed over mean MRI of the 19 alcohol-dependent patients at baseline in MNI space.

Those statistical choices are justified by 2 factors: first, the small sample size ( n = 19 for the cross-sectional analysis and n = 11 for the longitudinal analysis) and then the fact that the research can be considered as exploratory.
Only 11 of the 19 patients consented for a follow-up examination 6 months after the first one.

value: The total amount of alcohol consumed between baseline and follow-up negatively correlated with GM changes in the fusiform gyrus, cerebellar vermis, striatum, subthalamic region, amygdala, nucleus accumbens, supramarginal gyrus, cingulate gyrus, paracingulate gyrus, and anterior cingulate gyrus.

Limited alcohol consumption correlated with increased GM volumes in those regions; patients who resumed moderate alcohol consumption also showed positive regional brain-volume changes, indicating that some brain regions recover even in the absence of total abstinence.
There were no positive correlations between GM volumetric changes and interim drinking.

spans.text: The total amount of alcohol consumed between baseline and follow-up negatively correlated with GM changes in the fusiform gyrus (Fig. 4 A ), cerebellar vermis (Fig. 4 B ), striatum, subthalamic region, amygdala, and nucleus accumbens (Fig. 4 C ). Other smaller clusters included the supramarginal (Fig. 4 D ), cingulate (Fig. 4 E ), paracingulate (Fig. 4 F ), and anterior cingulate gyri (Fig. 4 G ). This indicated that limited alcohol consumption correlated with increased GM volumes in those regions.

Those statistical choices are justified by 2 factors: first, the small sample size ( n = 19 for the cross-sectional analysis and n = 11 for the longitudinal analysis) and then the fact that the research can be considered as exploratory.
Only 11 of the 19 patients consented for a follow-up examination 6 months after the first one.

value: Regression analysis between WM changes and the total amount of alcohol consumed between baseline and follow-up yielded significant negative-correlation clusters in the body and splenium of the corpus callosum and the superior corona radiata.

These findings reflect improvement with reduction of alcohol consumption or further degradation with resumption of heavy alcohol consumption in interhemispheric connectivity and connectivity within the limbic system.
A single significant positive-correlation cluster was observed in the deep white matter of the cerebellum.

All participants (patients and controls) underwent a high-resolution volumetric T1-weighted MRI scan (1.5T Signa Advance Echospeed; General Electric Milwaukee, WI) which consisted of a set of 128 adjacent axial planes parallel to the anterior commissure–posterior commissure line with a pixel size of 0.9375 mm 2 and slice thickness of 1.5 mm, using a spoiled gradient echo sequence (repetition time = 10.3 ms; echo time = 2.1 ms; field of view = 240 × 180 mm 2 ; matrix = 256 × 192).
